summary: David A. Dilworth is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo (1968), and held a post at Stony Brook University around 1970.

David A. Hall specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shoshin Ichishima in 1976 and earned his doctorate at UC Berkeley by 1990. He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and department chair at Montgomery College (attested 2019).
David Azzopardi is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

David B. Gray specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe. He was a fellow at Rice University and Associate Professor at Santa Clara University (attested 2008–2017).

David Bubna-Litic works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned his PhD from Western Sydney University (attested 2000) and was a Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney (attested 2000).

David Burton specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997) and served as Senior Lecturer in Theology and Religious Studies at Canterbury Christ Church University (attested 2010).

David Drewes is an indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Lawrence University, UW-Madison, and the University of Virginia (MA 1999, PhD 2006 under Karen C. Lang), he taught at Virginia, Indiana University (2006), and the University of Manitoba (attested 2009–2010).
David E. Cooper is a philosopher who studied at Highgate School (~1955–1960). He served as Professor of Philosophy at Durham University from 1986 to 2009.

David E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from UCLA. He taught at UCSB, UIUC, and the University of Hawaii, and held research posts at Nichibunken (attested 2006) and Oberlin College (attested 2010).
David Faure is a historian and sinologist. He completed his studies at the University of Hong Kong (~1966–1969) and Princeton University (~1970–1976).

David Fiordalis works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Carleton College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan (PhD attested 2008 under Luis Oscar Gómez), he became associate professor and department chair at Linfield University (attested 2017).

David Friedman was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He served as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS University of London (~1950–1970) and as Professor at the University of London (~1965–1970).

David Germano is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992 and served as Associate Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at the University of Virginia (attested 2000–2008).
David Gonsalez is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued traditional studies under Gen Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Gordon White is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his doctorate at the University of Chicago (~1981–1988) under Kali Charan Bahl. He held posts at Chicago (1984), the University of Virginia (~1986–1996), and UC Santa Barbara (~1996).

David J. Kalupahana was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Ceylon and earned a PhD at the University of London (~1964–1966). He taught at the University of Ceylon (~1959–1972) and the University of Hawaii (~1972–2014).

David Jones is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Hawaii. Attested in 2007, he served as a professor of philosophy in the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

David K. Wyatt was a historian who studied at Harvard (~1955–1959), Boston University (~1959–1960), and Cornell (~1960–1966). He held posts at SOAS (~1962–1968), the University of Michigan (~1968–1969), and Cornell University (~1969–2002).
David Kerman Tomlinson works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold (attested 2019) and held a post at Smith College.

David Kinsley was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Drew University (~1957–1961), Union Theological Seminary (~1961–1964), and the University of Chicago (~1964–1970), and held a post at McMaster University from 1969 to 2000.
